summary: A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, S. N. Balagangadhara studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch. He served as Director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and Co-Chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
An Indologist, S. N. Krishna was a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva (attested 2026).
S. N. Savadi was an Indology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.
An Indologist, Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and as Supervisor of Collations in 1942.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, S. Rajavelu served as Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and Professor in the Department of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).
S. S. Janaki was an Indologist who studied under Thomas Burrow (~1967–1971). She later served as a supervisor and guide at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute from around 1971 to 1999.

An Indology and philosophy scholar, S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942) at the University of Madras.

An Indologist and historian-archaeologist, S. Sankaranarayanan served as an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1985–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.
An Indologist, S. Sankararama Sastri held posts as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

S. Sepideh Hosseini, active in Indology, history, and archaeology, earned a bachelor's degree at Islamic Azad University, Damavand Branch, and completed an Indian language course at the University of Tehran.

An Indologist and historian, S. Srikanta Sastri studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna (~1923–1926). He held a post at the University of Mysore (~1926–1966) and taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.
An Indology and history-archaeology scholar, S. Swaminathan studied under J. Sundaram and served as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India until 2013.

A scholar of religious studies and sociocultural anthropology, Saba Mahmood studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University (PhD). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2018).

Working in Indology and philosophy, Sabine Löhr studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg (M.A.), where she worked under doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen and served as a research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft).
Sabriye Tenberken studied Tibetology at the University of Bonn (~1990–1997) and founded Braille Without Borders.

Saburō Hasegawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He taught Alan Watts and held teaching posts at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1957) and the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Working in computational linguistics and Indology, Sachin Kathale completed an M.Phil. at Jawaharlal Nehru University (ended 2007) and served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.

Sadajiro Sugiura studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. 1894), and Episcopal Divinity School. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the Army War College (1903), and Rikkyo University as lecturer (1907) and professor emeritus (1931–1932).

An Indology and philosophy scholar, Sadananda Das earned his BA at Central Sanskrit University and his MA and PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University. In 2005, he became a Lecturer (LfbA) at the University of Leipzig.
Saerji is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who has served as an Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026) at Peking University.
